steps.title: Prepare dissection medium
steps.instruction: To 200 mL MEM add 2 mL Penicillin‑Streptomycin (1.1 %), 5 mL HEPES buffer (2.5 %) and 2 mL 1 M Tris stock (1 %). Make 1 M Tris by dissolving Tris Base, adjust pH to 7.2 with 1 M HCl, sterile‑filter the combined solution through a 0.22 µm filter, cool to 4 °C and store at 4 °C for up to one month.

steps.title: Prepare complete culture medium
steps.instruction: To 500 mL DMEM/F12 add 55 mL fetal bovine serum (10 %), 5.5 mL Penicillin‑Streptomycin (1 %) and 5.5 mL GlutaMAX (1 %). Store at 4 °C for up to one month and warm for ~20 min in a 37 °C water bath before use.

steps.title: Prepare enzyme digestion mix
steps.instruction: For each gram of tissue prepare 10 mL mix: add 5 mL EBSS (20‑25 °C) to one vial of lyophilized papain and gently dissolve; prepare a DNase I stock of 1000 U/mL by diluting DNase I (20 000 U/mL) in HBSS and store at ‑20 °C for up to 12 months; to 8.65 mL Hibernate A medium add 1.25 mL dissolved papain and 100 µL DNase stock, warm to 37 °C and use within 1 h (do not store).

steps.title: Dissect brain and collect forebrain
steps.instruction: Euthanize an adult C57/BL6J mouse (12‑14 months) by cervical dislocation, decapitate and immediately immerse the head in 80 % ethanol; remove skin and skull with sterile dissection tools, place the brain into a petri dish containing ice‑cold (4 °C) dissection medium, quickly remove meninges with sharp forceps under a dissecting microscope, and dissect out the forebrain (discard mid‑brain, hind‑brain and hippocampus). Complete steps 2‑4 in <5 min to minimise cell death.

steps.title: Check initial microglia adherence
steps.instruction: 6–10 h after plating the digested tissue, examine the T25 or T75 flask under a bright‑field microscope; microglia appear phase‑bright and adherent to the bottom of the flask.

steps.title: Remove non‑adherent cells by tapping and washing
steps.instruction: Firmly and repeatedly tap the flask to detach non‑microglial cells while avoiding fluid entry into the filter at the neck; inspect the flask for any non‑phase‑bright adherent cells; discard all media containing floating cells and replace with fresh, warmed complete medium; repeat the tap‑wash cycle until only phase‑bright microglia remain (typically 2–5 washes, depending on tissue weight).

substeps.instruction: Check under microscope for non‑microglial adherent cells.
Remove all media with floating cells and add fresh warmed complete medium.
Repeat steps until only phase‑bright microglia are observed.

steps.title: Incubate purified microglia
steps.instruction: Incubate the purified microglial cultures for 2–5 days in fresh complete medium at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; if the medium becomes discoloured, replace half of it with fresh complete medium.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for isolating pure microglia cultures from aged adult mouse brains (12–14 months). However, our laboratory has utilized this protocol in the isolation of microglial cultures from mice as young as 4 months. Our laboratory also uses the same protocol to isolate microglia from adult human brain biopsy samples (Rustenhoven et al., 2016).CRITICAL: This protocol cannot be used for the isolation of microglia from newborn mouse pups (0–7 days old) due to the different adherent properties of microglia at this age.
